extracted.subtask_description: Writing short newspaper news items and follow-ups about crimes, arrests, and police incidents, using concise leads, specific facts, attribution, human detail and follow-up potential. The page provides multiple exemplar reports illustrating how to compose such items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full identification of persons
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide the full name, age, and residence of key individuals (suspects, victims, witnesses).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'Frederick A. White, fifty-six years old, who says he is a broker and lives at No. 345 West 116th street'; 'Laura Walsington, 20 years old, 14 West Thirty-second Street.' Use age and precise address where available to identify subjects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear statement of charge or alleged offense
rubrics_metrics.description: Say explicitly what the person was arrested for or accused of (e.g., swindling, forgery, embezzlement, burglary, hold-up).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'was arrested ... charged with swindling James H. Bums'; 'took to forgery.' Put the alleged crime early in the item for clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who arrested / investigating authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Attribute arrests and investigations to the arresting/detective/agency names (police, detectives, District Attorney's office).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'arrested yesterday by Detectives Fitzsimmons and Flood, of the District Attorney's office'; 'taken to police headquarters.' Naming the authority lends credibility and locates responsibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concrete specifics of the alleged crime
rubrics_metrics.description: Include precise particulars: amounts of money, property descriptions, dates of transactions, instruments used (checks, bonds), company names, titles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'lumber land ... worth $65,000'; 'two bonds for $25,000 each and three notes for $5,000 each'; 'thirty-seven diamonds, eight emeralds and eight pearls.' These details make the report informative and verifiable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence of events (chronology)
rubrics_metrics.description: Lay out the chronology: how the crime was committed, discovery, investigation, arrest, and immediate aftermath.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: the swindle story traces transfer of deeds, attempted collection, discovery that bonds weren't guaranteed, subsequent arrests; burglary stories show entry, action, discovery by occupant/child, and capture or escape. A clear timeline helps readers follow cause and effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence and investigative particulars
rubrics_metrics.description: Report physical or documentary evidence and investigative actions (fingerprints, found items, canceled checks, deposit slips, detectives' findings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'excellent set of finger prints on a hand mirror'; 'cancelled checks totalling $9,800 were produced from his safe.' Mentioning tangible evidence supports the story's factual basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attribution and source verbs
rubrics_metrics.description: Use attribution phrases when reporting claims or statements ('Bums says', 'the police say', 'he confessed').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'Bums says that through fraud and misrepresentation White obtained possession'; 'she confessed.' Proper attribution distinguishes reported facts from allegations or recollections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of direct quotations
rubrics_metrics.description: Include short, relevant direct quotes from suspects, victims, witnesses, or officials to convey voice, motive, and emotion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Suspect's plea 'I'll pay it all back' in the forgery case; robber blaming liquor 'I'd never have dreamed of robbing people if I hadn't been drunk.' Quotes add human interest and immediacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human-interest / personal background
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide concise personal or family background that explains motive or evokes sympathy (illness, poverty, prior occupations, marriages).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'Sister sick. No work. Money gone.'; Frank Green and Ruth Blair's courtship, marriage, and desperation; street-car bandit's sick wife and baby. Such details contextualize motives and impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scene and sensory description
rubrics_metrics.description: Use vivid, specific sensory or scene details where appropriate (smoke in the room, fainting passengers, window raised, crowd behavior) to dramatize the event.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'A cigarette on the floor, a room full of smoke'; the train riot: 'whistle screeching and hundreds of passengers yelling.' These make short items more compelling while remaining factual.

rubrics_metrics.name: Precise location and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Give exact or specific location details (addresses, intersections, stations, hotel names) and times or days when known.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'Pennsylvania Railroad Company's ferry house at Jersey City'; 'third avenue elevated train ... from One Hundred and Thirty-eighth street to One Hundred and Sixty-sixth street.' Location anchors the story geographically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior record or relevant history
rubrics_metrics.description: Mention prior arrests, past employment, or other history relevant to the present incident when it illuminates the story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'White was arrested, the police say, about five years ago, under the name of Wilce'; bank bookkeeper's prior jobs and salary trajectory. Such context can explain behavior and significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspect's explanation and remorse
rubrics_metrics.description: Report suspects' explanations, excuses, or expressions of remorse as part of the account, while attributing them properly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'I was going to be married and knew I would need a lot of money'; 'I'll pay it all back.' These statements provide color and are useful for readers' understanding; keep attribution clear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcome or immediate disposition
rubrics_metrics.description: Conclude with the immediate legal or practical disposition: held, charged, detained, in hospital, lodged in jail, or to be arraigned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'She is being held.'; 'Both will be charged with a felony, the prosecutor said last night.' Readers expect the immediate result of the incident.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flagging follow-up story potential
rubrics_metrics.description: Note when additional information could produce a striking follow-up (e.g., new developments, discovery of additional evidence, official statements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit example/note on page: 'NOTE — How, with additional information, a striking follow-up story can be written a few hours after the first story was published is well illustrated by the following two stories.' Use this to plan and label follow-ups.
